selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What happens in the sky when the time of ‘Isha begins?
questions.answer: The last light of day goes away, and night covers everything.

questions.question: What happens to the things people leave behind as time passes?
questions.answer: They fade away and are erased from this world.

questions.question: What does that fading away help a person remember?
questions.answer: That living things die and move on to another world.

questions.question: What does the passage say about this world compared with the hereafter?
questions.answer: This world is short and small, but the hereafter is lasting and great.

questions.question: Who is the only true One to love and worship?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: Why is Allah the only true One to worship, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because He easily changes night and day, seasons, and this world into the next.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Allah’s power over these changes?
questions.answer: It says He changes them easily, like turning pages.

questions.question: What main idea does this passage teach about the time of ‘Isha?
questions.answer: It reminds us of Allah’s power, the passing of this world, and the coming of the hereafter.

questions.question: If Allah can change winter to spring, what else can He change?
questions.answer: He can change this world into the hereafter.

questions.question: At nightfall, what disappears from the horizon?
questions.answer: The last bits of daylight.

questions.question: After that, what covers the universe?
questions.answer: The world of night.

questions.question: What season is named as the cold white one?
questions.answer: Winter.

questions.question: What season is described as green and decorated?
questions.answer: Summer.

questions.question: When old signs of people’s work disappear over time, what does that make us think about?
questions.answer: Death and going to a different world.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to this short world?
questions.answer: It will be destroyed and come to an end.

questions.question: What kind of world opens after this one?
questions.answer: A wide, everlasting, majestic world.

questions.question: Which is stronger in the passage: people and things in the world, or Allah?
questions.answer: Allah is stronger than all of them.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to show how easily Allah changes things?
questions.answer: It is like turning the pages of a book.

questions.question: What prayer time is this passage talking about?
questions.answer: The time of ‘Isha.

questions.question: What change happens first at that time?
questions.answer: Day ends and night begins.

questions.question: What does the change from day to night help us remember about the seasons?
questions.answer: It helps us remember summer changing into winter.

questions.question: What do disappearing traces from the past teach us?
questions.answer: Things in this world do not stay forever.

questions.question: Where do living things go after death, according to the passage?
questions.answer: To another world.

questions.question: How is this world described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is narrow, passing, and lowly.
